newsitem.title: USA: S.F. Fed's Parry sees stable demand for US assets.
newsitem.headline: S.F. Fed's Parry sees stable demand for US assets.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Robert Parry said on Tuesday he does not expect demand for U.S. securities to significantly waver.

"I frankly think it is unlikely we are going to see the appetite for U.S. securities slow down in a significant way," Parry said following a speech at a business conference in Eugene, Oregon sponsered by the San Francisco Fed.

Parry's remark was in response to reporters questions regarding Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's remark on Monday that currency volatility might cause his government to sell holdings of U.S. Treasuries and switch funds to gold.
"The (Hashimoto) comments had a profound impact on the stock market," Parry said, adding that the remarks were unlikely to be of long-term concern.
The Prime Minister's comments sparked a slide on Monday in the Dow Jones industrials index, which closed nearly 200 points lower but recovered on Tuesday to post modest gains.

Easing market tensions was a statement from Japan's Finance Ministry overnight that said Japan would continue to cooperate with the United States to stabilize foreign exchange rates and that Hashimoto regretted that his intentions had not been accurately conveyed.
Regarding the U.S. economy, Parry said a general consensus among economists shows the natural rate of unemployment currently stands between 5.50 and 5.75 percent.
"But here we are at 4.8 percent (unemployment rate) and not showing signs of inflation," Parry said.
Parry forecast a significant slowdown in second quarter U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) growth to "around two" percent from the first quarter's sizzling pace of 5.8 percent.
U.S. GDP growth will rise roughly three percent from the fourth quarter of 1996 to the same quarter in 1997, Parry added.
